title: My 3-Day London Adventure
disclaimer: This itinerary is an intelligent recommendation. Actual timings depend on opening hours, transport, and visitor preferences.

schedule.name: Big Ben and the Houses of Parliament
schedule.description: The majestic neo-Gothic Elizabeth Tower and seat of British parliamentary democracy along the Thames.
schedule.tips: Nearest Tube: Westminster (Jubilee, District, and Circle lines). Best views for photography are from the south end of Westminster Bridge or the Victoria Tower Gardens.

schedule.name: Borough Market Gourmet Lunch
schedule.description: Artisan hot street food, raclette, and farmhouse cheeses.

schedule.name: Westminster Abbey
schedule.description: The historic coronation church of the British monarchy and final resting place of monarchs, poets, and statesmen.
schedule.tips: Nearest Tube: Westminster or St James's Park. Photography is allowed outside service hours. Modest clothing is respectful in this active place of worship.

schedule.name: The London Eye
schedule.description: Europe's tallest cantilevered observation wheel offering breathtaking 360-degree vistas across London.
schedule.tips: Nearest Tube: Waterloo (Bakerloo, Northern, Jubilee, and Waterloo & City lines). Book fast-track tickets online in advance to bypass peak queue times.

schedule.name: Tower Bridge
schedule.description: London's world-renowned Victorian suspension bridge featuring high-level glass walkways and steam engine rooms.
schedule.tips: Nearest Tube: Tower Hill (Circle & District lines) or London Bridge. Combine your visit with the Tower of London and St Katharine Docks marina nearby.

schedule.name: Traditional Afternoon Tea
schedule.description: Warm clotted cream scones, delicate finger sandwiches, and fine tea.

schedule.name: Leadenhall Market
schedule.description: An ornate Victorian covered arcade with soaring wrought iron ribs and rich maritime history in the financial heart.
schedule.tips: Nearest Tube: Monument, Bank, or Aldgate. Visit on a weekday evening to experience the vibrant after-work city atmosphere, or Saturday morning for peaceful photography.

schedule.name: Borough Market
schedule.description: London's oldest and most celebrated gourmet food market, serving artisanal delicacies since 1756.
schedule.tips: Nearest Tube: London Bridge (Jubilee and Northern lines). Full market operates Wednesday to Sunday. Visit around 11:30 AM before the lunch rush crowds peak.

schedule.name: Buckingham Palace
schedule.description: The administrative headquarters of the British Monarch, famous for the ceremonial Changing of the Guard.
schedule.tips: Nearest Tube: Green Park, St James's Park, or Victoria. Arrive at least 45 minutes before 11:00 AM if you wish to secure a front-row view of the Guard Change.

schedule.name: Soho & Chinatown Dinner
schedule.description: Dim sum, Cantonese roast duck, or buzzing Italian pasta bars.

schedule.name: Soho & Chinatown
schedule.description: London's beating bohemian heart, packed with historic jazz clubs, legendary eateries, and vibrant theatre life.
schedule.tips: Nearest Tube: Leicester Square, Piccadilly Circus, or Tottenham Court Road. Pedestrianised in the evening with outdoor al-fresco dining across Kingly Street and Old Compton Street.

schedule.name: Neal's Yard
schedule.description: A kaleidoscope of vibrant painted facades, lush hanging plants, and organic cafés hidden down an alleyway.
schedule.tips: Nearest Tube: Covent Garden or Leicester Square. Accessed via narrow alleyways off Monmouth Street or Short's Gardens. Morning light is best for uncrowded photography.
